summary: Reproduced the multi-tokenizer BatchEmbeddingOutput repack dropping retraction_counts, cached_tokens_details, time_stats, and pooled_hidden_states. The repack now preserves those fields and correctly partitions both supported pooled-hidden-state IPC representations.

tests.what_was_measured: Regression reproduced on the recorded base: retraction_counts and pooled_hidden_states were None after embedding output repack; 2 failed, 7 passed. Raw output: reports/j-9301b111be10/raw/failing-before.txt

Final unit coverage of per-request fields, absent optional fields, non-stacked pooled states, and the scheduler's stacked pooled-state representation; 9 passed. Raw output: reports/j-9301b111be10/raw/final-unit.txt

On gfx950, splitting request index 1 from a stacked two-request tensor produced [7.0, 9.25], exactly equal to an independently constructed reference. Raw output: reports/j-9301b111be10/raw/gpu-stacked-pooled-hidden-state.txt
Repository formatting, lint, syntax, and registered-test validation hooks passed.

remaining_limitations: The Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B weights were not available, so the original HTTP server reproduction was not run end-to-end.
The prepared hardware is AMD gfx950 rather than the report's NVIDIA RTX A6000; this Python repack fix is device-independent, but the original NVIDIA environment was not reproduced.
The qualified tiny Llama fixture is not an embedding architecture and therefore was not used to claim end-to-end embedding-model validation.
No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
